narration.text: A grain farm's 2026 acreage report is filed before 15 July, as farmed and not as insured or as last year: a flooded corn plan replanted to soybeans, a 60 percent share lease, prevented planting, a crop after wheat, while rented-out, custom, sold, idle and future ground, wheat on file and a paid filing service are left alone. This is a chore for joanne Pellham, who farms corn and soybeans in central Iowa, on owned, cash-rented and share-leased ground, five days before the acreage reporting date. On the bench, she found 7 of 7 eligible items, worth 132 dollars and 65 cents of the 132 dollars and 65 cents there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 8 traps, and she walked past 8. She took 2 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes about 2 hours, so she was about 65 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
